ADDM Task ADDM:659179364_1_18205

          ADDM Report for Task 'ADDM:659179364_1_18205'
          ---------------------------------------------

Analysis Period
---------------
AWR snapshot range from 18204 to 18205.
Time period starts at 19-MAY-26 11.30.46 AM
Time period ends at 19-MAY-26 12.30.10 PM

Analysis Target
---------------
Database 'KRISHNA' with DB ID 659179364.
Database version during analysis period was 19.29.0.0.0.
Database version when ADDM was executed was 19.0.0.0.0.
All recommendations generated by ADDM are valid for database version 19.0.0.0.0, the version in which ADDM was executed.
ADDM performed an analysis of instance krishna, numbered 1 and hosted at
kirshnadb-pr.

Activity During the Analysis Period
-----------------------------------
Total database time was 37884 seconds.
The average number of active sessions was 10.63.

Summary of Findings
-------------------
   Description                      Active Sessions      Recommendations
                                    Percent of Activity
   -------------------------------  -------------------  ---------------
1  Session Connect and Disconnect   1.67 | 15.68         1
2  Soft Parse                       1.62 | 15.21         2
3  Shared Pool Latches              .67 | 6.34           1
4  Hard Parse Due to Invalidations  .52 | 4.85           1
5  Top SQL Statements               .48 | 4.52           1
6  "User I/O" wait Class            .22 | 2.1            0


~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~


          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.67 active sessions, 15.68% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.67 active sessions, 15.68% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.62 active sessions, 15.21% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.62 active sessions, 15.21% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.62 active sessions, 15.21% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 3: Shared Pool Latches
Impact is .67 active sessions, 6.34% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Contention for latches related to the shared pool was consuming significant
database time.
Waits for "latch: shared pool" amounted to 5% of database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .67 active sessions, 6.34% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the cause for latch contention using the given blocking
      sessions or modules.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 9077 and serial number 28385 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 14% of this recommendation's
      benefit.
   Rationale
      The session with ID 5348 and serial number 57153 in instance number 1
      was the blocking session responsible for 12% of this recommendation's
      benefit.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Concurrency" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .68 active sessions, 6.41% of total activity.


Finding 4: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .52 active sessions, 4.85% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .52 active sessions, 4.85% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 1.1 active sessions, 10.31% of total activity.


Finding 5: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .48 active sessions, 4.52% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Recommendation 1: SQL Tuning
   Estimated benefit is .48 active sessions, 4.52% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "56980hjqxb68r" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 56980hjqxb68r.
         BEGIN PKG_COMMON_PROC.PROC_SETENV(:1,:2); END;
   Rationale
      The SQL Tuning Advisor cannot operate on PL/SQL statements.
   Rationale
      Database time for this SQL was divided as follows: 4% for SQL execution,
      43% for parsing, 53% for PL/SQL execution and 0% for Java execution.


Finding 6: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is .22 active sessions, 2.1% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.
The SGA was adequately sized.

   No recommendations are available.

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.38 active sessions, 19.14% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.38 active sessions, 19.14% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.23 active sessions, 17.03% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.23 active sessions, 17.03% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.23 active sessions, 17.03% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "200" during the
      analysis period.

Impact is .42 active sessions, 5.81% of total activity.

   Action

Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .21 active sessions, 2.95% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Estimated benefit is .21 active sessions, 2.95% of total activity.
